thread:
maya: Heads up — on the canary for the new quota dashboard I see org A's daily usage numbers briefly showing up under org B when I switch tabs fast. :thinking:
kevin: Wait, under the canary only? or main too?
maya: Only on canary (edge rollout group). Haven't seen it on prod orgs in stable. Repro is pretty consistent if you: 1) open dashboard A, 2) quickly switch to dashboard B before the widgets finish hydrating.
oliver: Can you paste the router debug output when that happens? I'm wondering if the route context is getting swapped between requests.
maya: Here's a raw excerpt from router debug around the moment:```[2025-11-02T15:12:03Z] req_id=abcd1234 method=GET path=/internal/dashboard/render downstream=frontend headers={X-Org: 9482, X-Workspace: 33, X-Request-Id: abcd1234} matched_route=dashboard-v2 canary=true user=maya
[2025-11-02T15:12:04Z] req_id=abcd1234 child_req_id=efgh5678 method=GET path=/internal/metrics/fetch headers={X-Org: 8811, X-Workspace: 88, X-Request-Id: efgh5678} matched_route=metrics-proxy canary=true user=backend
```
zoe: Hmm the metrics fetch call has a different X-Org header. That smells like header mutation in the proxy layer or a shared header map leaking across async tasks.
kevin: This mirrors a class of bugs we fixed last quarter, but that was about auth tokens not headers. Two immediate hypotheses: (A) middleware that copies context isn't cloning per-request state and reuses a header map, (B) our canary routing path uses a different sidecar that normalizes headers differently leading to collision.
samir: Can we confirm which component injects X-Org vs X-Workspace? I thought the gateway set X-Workspace and the internal proxy set X-Org for compatibility. That duplication seems dangerous.
oliver: Right — current flow: edge-gateway -> auth-proxy (attaches X-Workspace) -> org-normalizer (attaches X-Org) -> service. Canary uses a lightweight org-normalizer shim that we deployed last week. If that shim mutates a shared object, concurrent requests could cross-pollinate.
maya: Repro steps attached: quick gif + request ids. When it occurs, the dashboard shows rows with org name and metrics from a different org for about 700ms before the widgets re-render. UX impact is high — customers could snapshot wrong numbers. :grimacing:
kevin: Action plan suggestion: 1) revert shim on canary immediately, 2) add assert in org-normalizer that headers object is immutable per-request, 3) add unit test for concurrent header mutation, 4) add a lightweight middleware gate to drop requests where X-Org/X-Workspace mismatch detected. Thoughts?
zoe: +1 to revert first. Also we should instrument a histogram of X-Org vs auth-subject mismatches to catch silent leaks.
samir: I can patch the shim with a defensive copy today (simple fix). But we should discuss the longer-term API: using both X-Org and X-Workspace is ambiguous — propose we standardize on X-Redwood-Org to avoid collisions with downstream proxies that use generic X-Org headers.
oliver: I'd prefer minimal surface change for now. Standardizing header names is a breaking change across infra and 3rd-party integrations. If we introduce X-Redwood-Org we need a migration period where both are accepted and validated.
kevin: Internal API debate: 1) rename to X-Redwood-Org now (fast, more explicit) vs 2) keep X-Org but namespace it at the gateway layer (safer, slower). Vote?
maya: For immediate safety: revert, patch shim, instrument. For API, favor namespacing (X-Redwood-Org) but roll out slowly with telemetry.
sre-bot: deploybot: Revert PR #4521 to canary cluster scheduled — started. :white_check_mark:
samir: I'll open a PR for the defensive-copy fix and add a concurrent test. Will also add telemetry for mismatches. ETA: end of day.
kevin: I'll drive the header-naming RFC. Let's include rollout UX notes: console should show when a widget's data might be stale during fast tab switching (fade + loading state) so users don't misread transient cross-talk.
zoe: Good idea — small UX change could mitigate surface impact while infra patch lands.
maya: Thanks all. tagging @kevin @samir for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
kevin: I'll post the RFC link here once drafted. Samir, ping me when PR is ready and we'll cherry-pick to hotfix branch if tests pass.
maya: Verified revert removed immediate repro on canary, monitoring for recurrences. :eyes:
